title: Lightly Peppery Middle Eastern Morcilla Tagine
description: A lightly peppery and flavorful one-pot Middle Eastern dish featuring morcilla, made pescatarian-friendly and cooked to perfection in a tandoor clay pot. This unique tagine combines the richness of morcilla with the brightness of Middle Eastern spices.
instructions: Cook the sliced morcilla in a large tandoor clay pot over medium heat until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the morcilla from the pot and set aside, leaving the drippings behind.
Add the olive oil to the pot and saute the chopped onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Stir in the shio-koji, ground cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, cooking for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the morcilla to the pot and reduce the heat to low, simmering covered for 20 minutes.
Stir in the chopped parsley and cook for an additional 5 minutes, or until the morcilla is heated through.
Serve the morcilla tagine hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
